subject: Delhi's Yamuna — the money, the sewage arithmetic, and CPCB's monthly 2025 readings
transcription: Read off the source release, once, and COMMITTED. Every figure below is quoted from it. The derived block states its own arithmetic so any reader can repeat it.

source.name: Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India
source.publication: PROGRESS IN CLEANING OF YAMUNA RIVER — written reply in Lok Sabha
source.question: Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1949
source.answered_by: Minister of State for Jal Shakti, Shri Raj Bhushan Choudhary
source.why_this_document: A parliamentary answer is better provenance than a feed: it is numbered, dated, attributable to a named minister, and the government is answerable for it. Under D-13.6 the figure is quoted, the document is attached, and no inference is drawn beyond the arithmetic.
source.cadence: per session — a document, not a feed

monthly_readings_2025.role: CPCB's own monthly monitoring, published inside the reply. Better cadence than the annual NWMP compilation, and it corroborates it.

limits_as_printed.authority: Primary Water Quality Criteria, printed in the reply's own table header

monthly_readings_2025.bdl_note: The government writes dissolved oxygen at three of the four stations as '0.3(BDL)'. BDL is BELOW DETECTION LIMIT. 0.3 is not a measurement of how much oxygen is present; it is the smallest number the method can report. The correct reading is 'at or below 0.3', and the honest word is not 'low' but 'absent'.

stations.station: RIVER YAMUNA AT OKHLA BARRAGE D/S
stations.position: where the river leaves the city

stations.station: RIVER YAMUNA AT ASGARPUR (AFTER CONFLUENCE OF SHAHDARA DRAIN AND TUGHLAKABAD DRAIN)
stations.position: immediately after two of Delhi's drains join it

gaps: March dissolved oxygen is blank at Nizamuddin and Okhla Barrage in the source table. It is left null here and the container that would show it renders nothing. It is not carried forward from February and it is not interpolated.
March faecal coliform at Nizamuddin is printed as 'NA' in the source. Recorded as null.
Palla has no March row at all in the source.

sewage.authority: Delhi Jal Board, via the reply
sewage.untreated_note: the reply's own words: 'about 641 MLD of sewage remains untreated and enters the river or drainage network'

derived.note: Every item here is arithmetic on the numbers above and states its own sum. Nothing is inferred beyond the operation shown, per D-13.6.

not_treated_to_standard_mld.reading: The headline figure in circulation is 641 MLD untreated. But 3,596 MLD is generated and only 2,014 MLD is treated to the standard, so 1,582 MLD — forty-four per cent of Delhi's sewage — reaches the river either untreated or treated below the discharge standard. Both numbers are in the same paragraph of the same reply.

idle_capacity_mld.reading: Delhi has 519 MLD of sewage treatment capacity built and not being used, at the same time as 641 MLD of sewage goes untreated. The idle capacity is 81 per cent of the untreated flow.

non_compliant_stp_share_pct.reading: Fourteen of Delhi's thirty-seven working sewage plants do not meet the discharge standard set by Delhi's own pollution control committee.

cost_per_mld_crore.reading: The completed Namami Gange work in Delhi cost about 1.54 crore rupees for each million litres a day of capacity.

utilisation_2025_pct.reading: Of the money allocated for Yamuna cleaning since January 2025, 77 per cent had been spent by the date of the reply.

gpi_non_compliance_pct.reading: Nearly a third of the working grossly polluting industries inspected on the Yamuna's main stem were breaking their discharge conditions or operating without valid consent. Nine were ordered closed.

money.what_is_not_here: This reply covers Namami Gange work in Delhi and the money moved since January 2025. It is NOT the total ever spent on the Yamuna. Figures of 6,500 crore and 8,000 crore circulate widely, sourced to a parliamentary panel via journalism rather than to the panel's own document. Under this site's rules those belong in the coverage band as reporting, never in the money band as data. Closing this properly needs the panel report itself.

industry.by: CPCB, with joint teams including IITs, NITs and DPCC/SPCBs
industry.the_scale_note: 1.33 MLD of industrial discharge against 641 MLD of untreated sewage. On these official numbers, industry is not the main thing in this river — the city's own sewage is. That is worth stating plainly because it is not what most coverage implies.

caveats: A parliamentary reply is a statement by the government about itself. It is authoritative as a record of what the government says, and it is not independently audited.
'0.3(BDL)' is below the detection limit. It is a floor, not a measurement, and must never be rendered as 0.0 or as a precise value.
Capacity utilised is not the same as sewage treated to standard, and the reply gives both. Conflating them overstates treatment by 941 MLD.
The monthly table covers four stations. CPCB's annual compilation covers seven in Delhi. The two are consistent where they overlap and are published as two sources, not merged.
Blank and 'NA' cells in the source are recorded as null and render nothing. They are never interpolated.
